concept_name: Metallic Bonding — A Lattice of Cores in a Shared Electron Sea
section: Class 11 Chemistry Ch.4 'Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure', §4.3 — Metallic Bond
source_book: NCERT Chemistry Class 11, Ch.4 'Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure' — chapter-index scope reference only (metallic bonding: brief qualitative mention; the Solid State unit that would carry lattice/electron-sea depth is removed from the rationalised syllabus, so this concept's depth exceeds the current CBSE floor by design). Teaching, sequence, examples and phrasing authored from first principles. NCERT Exemplar consulted for misconception beliefs only (the per-atom electron-ownership belief; the fast-electron conduction belief). No problem text, figure or prose imported. Desk 3, concept 2 of 2 in the Phase-0 bonding wave, on the bonding_scene scenario (field_3d), same scenario as Desk 2's ionic_bonding. Only STATE_1 (lattice_grow) is LIVE today on E3a; STATE_2-STATE_7 are authored COMPLETE against the sealed Checkpoint-A design (docs/skeletons/metallic_bonding_skeleton.md, cycle 2 of 2, founder-proxy DESIGN_OK) and become live the moment the E3b field3d-surgeon dispatch (docs/notes/metallic_bonding_E3b_request.md) merges -- see the top-level _e3b_pending block below for the exact per-state capability map and the contract items (five original plus a coined shift.plane value and a declared STATE_6 retiming) this file authors against before they are formally decided. Advisory cross-reference (no pill wiring, Gate 8b all-or-nothing forbids linking chemistry concepts into the physics registration sites): STATE_4's slow-drift beat is the same two-speed picture (fast random motion vs a very slow net drift) taught by the shipped physics concept drift_velocity (STATE_3/STATE_4) on a copper wire.
concept_tier_note: Tier: diamond (💎), capabilities 1 + 3 + 4. A whiteboard draws one atom losing an electron and stops there. It cannot show a shared swarm roaming a whole 3D lattice with no electron attached to any atom (capability 1), a drift bias appearing under a field while the fast random motion carries no current (capability 3), or a layer slide that HOLDS -- visibly re-seating into the same pattern one row over -- exactly where the salt crystal split (capability 4).

real_world_anchor.primary: A metal spoon bends without breaking, while a grain of table salt always shatters — because the same one-layer slide that splits the ionic crystal leaves the metal's shared electron sea sitting between the layers, holding the metal whole.
real_world_anchor.secondary: The copper wire inside any charger cable carries current as a slow drift in the same kind of delocalised electron sea described here — the wire's free electrons also carry the heat you feel in a warm cable.

aha_moment.statement: No electron in a metal belongs to one atom; one shared sea holds it together.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: One tagged electron crosses the whole block, passing many cores, and never returns to the atom it left.

n_e.name: free-electron number density, sodium
n_e.note: derived n = rho*N_A*z/M at 298 K, rho=0.968 g/cm3, M=22.99 g/mol, z=1 (chemistry block Duty 2)

mu_Na.name: electron mobility, sodium (derived, not measured directly)
mu_Na.note: mu = sigma/(n e), sigma_Na ~2.1e7 S/m, n=2.5e28 m^-3 (chemistry block Duty 3)

field.name: applied field control (dimensionless slider)
field.note: STATE_4 core; maps LINEARLY to E = 0 to 0.04 V/m

v_d.name: electron drift speed
v_d.note: CORRECTED full-scale value 2.1e-4 m/s (the dispatch brief's 1e-4 was an arithmetic slip, chemistry block Duty 3). Live v_d = 0 m/s exactly at field = 0, never a dash or a stale value.

like_contacts.name: like-charge nearest-neighbour contacts left unscreened (D-7 definition)
like_contacts.note: reads 0 at EVERY offset on the metal (the sea screens every contact, before and after) -- design expectation; any nonzero reading is a build defect (D-7), never a tuning target

valence.name: free electrons per atom control (STATE_6 stepped slider)
valence.note: stepped 1 -> 2 -> 3, never fractional; sea count = 35 x valence dots; core charge label steps +1 -> +2 -> +3

like_contacts.formula: screened like-charge nearest-neighbour contacts (D-7 definition) -- reads 0 at every offset on this cation-only, sea-screened lattice

atomisation_trend.formula: y = dH_at (Na 107, Mg 146, Al 326) plotted against x = valence (1, 2, 3) -- points only, no fit line authored

formulas.charge_balance_S2: sum(q_site) + sum(q_released_dot) = 0 at every instant of the release ramp
formulas.charge_balance_S6: sum(q_core) = 35 x valence ; sum(q_sea) = -(35 x valence) ; net 0 at every step

constraints: atoms and charge both balance in the S2 half-equation Na -> Na+ + e- (no state symbols -- the electron leaves one core to join the shared sea entirely inside the solid, no phase change)
total charge: sum(q_sites) + sum(q_released_dots) = 0 at every instant of S2's ionisation ramp, and sum(q_core) + sum(q_sea) = 0 at every S6 valence step
n(free electrons released per site) = BS_VALENCE[species] exactly -- never a fractional electron
v_d = mu_Na * E_field holds at every field-slider position, including exactly v_d = 0 m/s (live) at field = 0
like_contacts reads 0 at every shift offset on this cation-only, sea-screened lattice -- any nonzero reading is a build defect (D-7), never a tuning target

dH_at is monotonic in valence (Na < Mg < Al) on the S6 trend axis, with each step well above the +-5 kJ/mol source-spread noise band -- non-monotonicity or a collapsed step is a ratification failure, never a display choice
neutral-metal and ionic radii on this scenario share ONE linear-in-pm scale (BS_RADIUS_PM), never the legibility-compressed MG_ELEMENTS scale

STATE_1.title: Atoms pack in a regular lattice
STATE_1.label: Sodium atoms pack into a repeating bcc lattice — the same spacing continues through the whole block

scene_composition.text: One solid block of metal
The same spacing repeats everywhere
This block is a tiny corner of the metal
Atoms drawn smaller to show the pattern

tts_sentences.text_en: Every solid metal is atoms packed in a repeating pattern.
Watch sodium atoms settle into rows — each new atom sits at the same spacing as the last.
The block keeps this exact pattern in every direction, through the whole piece of metal.

STATE_2.title: Outer electrons come free
STATE_2.label: Every atom's outer electron leaves at once; the cores become smaller positive ions

scene_composition.text: The same block as before
Each atom releases one electron
The cores are now positive ions

tts_sentences.text_en: Sodium holds its outer electron weakly.
Watch: every atom in the block releases that one electron at once.
The freed electrons stay inside the metal — for now each sits beside the ion it left.
Every core is now a positive ion, smaller than its atom.

STATE_3.title: One shared sea holds all the cores
STATE_3.label: The freed electrons roam the whole crystal — no electron belongs to any one atom, and the shared sea is the metallic bond

scene_composition.text: The same block, now with free electrons
This electron is not attached to any atom
The sea of electrons holds the cores together

tts_sentences.text_en: Now watch one electron.
It moves right across the block, past core after core, and it never goes back to the atom it left.
Every free electron does this — one shared sea through the whole crystal.
The pull between the positive cores and this negative sea is the metallic bond.

misconception_watch.belief: In a metal each electron still belongs to its own atom
misconception_watch.visual_counter: one tagged electron crosses the whole block, passing core after core, and never returns to the atom it left
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The outer electrons are shared by the whole crystal — no electron is attached to any one atom.

STATE_4.title: Field on: a slow drift carries current
STATE_4.label: An electric field adds a slow net drift on top of the sea's random motion — that drift is the current, and the same sea carries heat

scene_composition.text: The same block, sea established
The same random motion as before
The stronger the field, the faster the drift

tts_sentences.text_en: Connect this metal in a circuit and an electric field appears through the block at once.
Watch the sea: the same random motion, plus a very slow net drift along the field — the counter shows how slow.
That slow shared drift is the electric current.
The same free electrons also carry heat through the metal.

misconception_watch.belief: Conduction is fast because the electrons move fast
misconception_watch.visual_counter: the field appears everywhere at once while the drift counter shows a very slow live value — the fast random motion carries no current; the slow shared drift is the current
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: The field acts on every electron at once; each electron itself only drifts very slowly — that slow shared drift is the current.

STATE_5.title: Layers slide and the metal holds
STATE_5.label: The same one-site layer slide that split salt leaves the metal whole, because the sea screens every position — metals bend and draw instead of shattering

scene_composition.text: The sea sits between every pair of cores
Salt split at this step — the metal holds.
The pattern after the slide is the same pattern as before.

tts_sentences.text_en: In salt, this same one-site slide lined up like charges and the crystal split.
Slide the metal's top layer.
The counter stays at zero: the sea sits between the cores at every position.
The layer settles into the same pattern one row over, so metals can be bent and drawn into wires.

STATE_6.title: More electrons per atom, stronger metal
STATE_6.label: Keeping the same lattice, more free electrons per atom and higher core charge raise the enthalpy of atomisation from sodium to magnesium to aluminium

scene_composition.text: The same block and cell throughout
Each step: one more electron, one more charge
More charge, more sea: a stronger hold

tts_sentences.text_en: Keep the same lattice and change one thing: how many electrons each atom gives to the sea.
One, then two, then three.
Each step also raises the charge on every core.
The chart shows the energy needed to pull one mole of atoms out: it climbs steeply.
More shared electrons, stronger metal.

STATE_7.label: Pick a metal, and drag field or layer shift to see the lattice and its sea respond

Drag field or layer shift
Watch the readouts respond

regeneration_variants.label: Same lattice-and-sea reasoning, potassium instead of sodium
regeneration_variants.physical_world: Potassium's single outer electron forms the same delocalised sea in a bcc lattice of potassium cations — the same pack, release, roam, drift and layer-slide story, with a lower melting point and a larger cell edge.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical single-electron delocalisation mechanism, identical bcc lattice, identical slow-drift conduction and identical layer-slide malleability; only the specific metal's cell edge, atomisation enthalpy and melting point change.
